title: Cross-validation folds that keep each depot whole

blocks.text: A delivery company tunes its routing solver on last year's models, one per depot per month. Months of one depot share roads and customers, so if January's model of a depot is in the training set and February's in the test set, the test is not a test: the tuner has, in effect, seen it. The team uses $`k`$-fold cross-validation (tune on all folds but one, test on the one left out, and repeat for each fold), and every depot must sit wholly inside one fold.

With $`N`$ the instance names, $`g(n)`$ the group (depot) of instance $`n`$, and $`G`$ the groups in sorted order $`g_0, g_1, \dots`$, write before you code: which fold group $`g_j`$ goes to, which instances fold $`f`$ holds, and, for a split into a training set $`A`$ and a test set $`B`$, the set of groups that leak.

Write `folds(names, group_of, k)` and `leaks(train, test, group_of)` in `validation.py`. `folds` returns `k` lists, the names in each sorted; `leaks` returns a set of groups. The tests pass small lists; no solver runs. About six lines.

cases.says: depots are dealt to the folds round-robin, in name order
a depot with models on both sides of a split is reported as a leak
no depot's models are split across folds
every model lands in exactly one fold
the folds are the same whatever order the names arrive in
asking for more folds than depots gives that many folds, some empty

origin.section: Hold Out Whole Groups the Tuner Never Sees
